[Our approach]{.cgm-eyebrow}

## Curiosity in the field. Insight in the data.
:::

::: {.cgm-intro}
The Computational Geomorphology and Modeling Lab brings quantitative and statistical approaches to questions about environmental processes. Coastal and aeolian systems are a major research focus; data science, statistical reasoning, and reproducible computation are central to how we work.

We combine field measurements and high-resolution topography with inferential statistics, machine learning, and time-series analysis to examine patterns, test hypotheses, and evaluate uncertainty.
:::

:::

[Inside the workflow]{.cgm-eyebrow}

## How do we turn a question into understanding?

Open a method to explore how it fits into our research.
:::

::: {.cgm-methods}

::: {.callout-note collapse="false" appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## 01 — Observe & measure

Field measurements, LiDAR, UAS-derived surfaces, and terrestrial laser scanning help us document environmental conditions and landform morphology across space and time.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## 02 — Organize & explore

R and GIS support data management, visualization, spatial analysis, and reproducible workflows that make complex datasets easier to investigate.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## 03 — Model & evaluate

Inferential statistics, machine learning, and time-series analysis help us test hypotheses, explore nonlinear relationships, assess uncertainty, and evaluate model performance.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" icon="false"}
## 04 — Interpret & communicate

We connect analytical results to environmental processes and communicate what the evidence supports, including its limits and implications for environmental management.
:::

:::

Students build skills in data collection, coding, quantitative reasoning, and interpreting environmental datasets.
